name: Red-Blue Operations (Easy Version)
description: The only difference between easy and hard versions is the maximum values of $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ . You are given an array, consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. Initially, all elements are red. You can apply the following operation to the array multiple times. During the $$$i$$$-th operation, you select an element of the array; then: if the element is red, it increases by $$$i$$$ and becomes blue; if the element is blue, it decreases by $$$i$$$ and becomes red. The operations are numbered from $$$1$$$, i. e. during the first operation some element is changed by $$$1$$$ and so on. You are asked $$$q$$$ queries of the following form: given an integer $$$k$$$, what can the largest minimum in the array be if you apply exactly $$$k$$$ operations to it? Note that the operations don't affect the array between queries, all queries are asked on the initial array $$$a$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 1000$$$) — the number of elements in the array and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). The third line contains $$$q$$$ integers $$$k_1, k_2, \dots, k_q$$$ ($$$1 \le k_j \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each query, print a single integer — the largest minimum that the array can have after you apply exactly $$$k$$$ operations to it.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1832D1 — Red-Blue Operations (Easy Version) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
